definitions.explanation: An officer rank above {中尉|ちゅうい} and below {少佐|しょうさ}. In army and air force usage this corresponds to "captain"; in navy usage to "lieutenant." In the Self-Defense Forces the equivalent rank is called {一等陸尉|いっとうりくい}/{一等海尉|いっとうかいい}/{一等空尉|いっとうくうい}.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{大尉|たいい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{昇進|しょうしん}→昇進：04553_shoushin⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
{大尉|たいい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{部隊|ぶたい}→部隊：28119_butai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{率|ひき}いている→率いる：10879_hikiiru⟧。
examples.english: A captain is leading the unit.

examples.japanese: {戦争映画|せんそうえいが}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{主人公|しゅじんこう}→主人公：11404_shujinkou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{陸軍|りくぐん}→陸軍：19089_rikugun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{若|わか}い{大尉|たいい}だった。
examples.english: The protagonist of the war film was a young army captain.

notes:
Compound of {大|たい} (great) + {尉|い} (officer of the lower commissioned ranks). The {尉|い} series of ranks comprises:
- {少尉|しょうい}: second lieutenant (lowest commissioned rank)
- {中尉|ちゅうい}: first lieutenant
- {大尉|たいい}: captain (army/AF) / lieutenant (navy)

Note on homophones: {大尉|たいい} is a homophone of ⟦{退位|たいい}→退位：19973_taii⟧ (abdication). Context normally disambiguates.

USAGE:
- Most often encountered in historical contexts, fiction (war films, novels), and discussion of foreign militaries
- In the modern Japanese Self-Defense Forces, the rank is officially called {一等陸尉|いっとうりくい} (army), {一等海尉|いっとうかいい} (navy), {一等空尉|いっとうくうい} (air force) — often shortened to {一尉|いちい}
